theorem: Let (X*,Z*) be any balanced Hermitian Clifford pair and let targets be X0=alpha X*, Z0=beta Z* with alpha,beta>0. For every competing Clifford pair (X,Z), the objective excess is exactly alpha||X-X*||_F^2+beta||Z-Z*||_F^2. It is strictly positive unless both factors equal the target pair. Hence the joint nearest-factor problem has one global minimizer in every balanced dimension. The two positive coefficients are simultaneous coercive gaps; the theorem is invariant under arbitrary common unitary conjugation.
